data.narrative:
Gridware is a Series B-stage climate and energy company that has raised $97.5M to date across its founding team of Abdulrahman Bin Omar, Timothy Barat, and Hall Chen. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable, primarily positioned in adjacent stages within the energy transition and materials technology sectors.

Two valuation methodologies prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $97.5M total raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-later-stage advancement, yielding $185M. Peer-median analysis anchors on three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C)—producing a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating these two methods across their respective inputs and uncertainty bands supports a valuation range of $157M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median point of $593M. The stage-progression method anchors a conservative floor, while the peer-median approach reflects the valuation multiples observed in climate-tech at comparable development stages. Key uncertainties include the precise stage positioning relative to the peer set, which skews toward Series C, and the absence of transaction precedent for Gridware's specific technology focus within the sample. The wide range reflects appropriate skepticism about peer comparability in early-stage climate tech.
